hypotheses.cause: External partner kyc-agency is experiencing severe latency degradation and an upstream processing backlog, drastically reducing decision webhook dispatches and causing new KYC applications to accumulate in pending status.
hypotheses.rationale: Agency latency p95 surged from 1700ms to over 4000ms starting at 09:30 UTC (ev_10), with kyc-service logging multiple slow submission warnings taking between 5.0s and 7.4s (ev_13, ev_14, ev_16). Furthermore, only 29 webhook requests arrived at /hooks/kyc across the entire 3.5-hour incident window (ev_23) despite over 1300 pending KYCs accumulating (ev_11, ev_19), while the few webhooks that did arrive were processed successfully with HTTP 200 (ev_25). This aligns with past external agency backlog incidents (PIR-2006, PIR-1705 in ev_1). Confidence is limited to 0.65 because message-queue metrics timed out and a consumer rebalance was observed.

hypotheses.cause: A rebalance on the message-queue kyc-hooks consumer group at 09:38 UTC left one or more consumer partitions stuck or unconsumed, preventing pending KYC status transitions from being applied.
hypotheses.rationale: At 09:38 UTC, message-queue logged a WARN event showing consumer group kyc-hooks rebalanced when 1 of 3 consumers left the group (ev_18), exactly two minutes before kyc_pending_count began climbing at 09:40 UTC (ev_11, ev_19). This mechanism matches SEV2 incident PIR-2014 where agency-approved KYCs stayed pending after a rebalance (ev_1). However, agency latency degradation began 8 minutes earlier at 09:30 UTC (ev_10), incoming webhook volume at /hooks/kyc was abnormally low at only 29 lines (ev_23), and webhooks continued to process across hyd-a and mum-a (ev_25), keeping confidence at 0.35.

findings.summary: No deployments, configuration changes, or infrastructure modifications occurred for kyc-service, database, or message-queue in the investigation window (08:00–12:30 UTC) or in the preceding two days. Past incident history shows two historical causes for KYC pending spikes: internal consumer stalls on message-queue (PIR-2014) and external KYC agency maintenance/backlogs (PIR-1705, PIR-2006). The next phase should check message-queue consumer lag and kyc-service webhook metrics and logs.

observations.statement: No deployments, configuration changes, feature-flag changes, or infrastructure modifications occurred in kyc-service, database, or message-queue during the 2026-09-10 08:00:00Z to 12:30:00Z window, nor in the preceding two days (2026-09-08 to 2026-09-10).

Across all services between 08:00Z and 12:30Z on 2026-09-10, only three unrelated changes took place: assistant-orchestrator config change at 09:38 UTC (CHG-48483), debit-worker deploy at 09:58 UTC (CHG-48496), and mf-order-service feature flag update at 10:23 UTC (CHG-48502).

kyc-service depends downstream on database (critical datastore, timeout 1000ms), kyc-agency (critical external_api, timeout 5000ms, retries 1), and message-queue (critical async). Upstream, it receives requests from api-gateway (sync, timeout 3000ms) and status webhooks from external partner kyc-agency to /hooks/kyc.

Three past KYC pending incidents were identified: PIR-2014 (SEV2, 2026-08-21), where agency-approved KYCs stayed pending because the kyc_webhooks message-queue consumer stuck after a rebalance (resolved by restarting consumers); PIR-1705 (SEV3, 2026-09-04), caused by scheduled KYC agency maintenance; and PIR-2006 (SEV3), caused by an external KYC agency processing backlog.

Because there were no internal releases, config, or infra changes around the 09:40 UTC onset, the incident was not triggered by a recent deployment or configuration update. Historical precedent points to two competing hypotheses: an internal consumer stall on message-queue (as in PIR-2014) vs an external delay/backlog from kyc-agency (as in PIR-1705/PIR-2006).
